-== Deprecated: Pipe (kind: Pipe) support
-The YAML DSL can load Camel K `kind: Pipe` resources (formerly `KameletBinding`), typically from a
-`.pipe.yaml` file, converting the source, steps and sink into a regular route when the file is loaded.
-This is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Loading a Pipe file now logs a deprecation
-warning. Write a plain Camel route instead, which is more expressive (any EIP, multiple routes per file,
-error handling and route configuration) and is what the tooling, catalog and validator work on. See the
-xref:manual::camel-4x-upgrade-guide-4_23.adoc[Camel 4.23 upgrade guide] for an example of the equivalent route.

+=== Camel K Pipe and Integration resources are removed (camel bind)
+Camel works with routes as its abstraction. The support for the Camel K resources, deprecated in Camel 4.19 (`camel
+bind`) and 4.23 (Pipe in the YAML DSL), is removed:
+* The YAML DSL no longer loads `kind: Pipe` (or `KameletBinding`) resources with `apiVersion: camel.apache.org/v1`,
+  and `.pipe.yaml` is no longer a file extension of the YAML DSL.
+* The `camel bind` command is removed, and so are `camel init --pipe` and the Integration CR template of `camel init`
+  (`.integration.yaml`). `camel run` no longer takes a file with a Pipe.
+Write a Camel route instead: the source of the Pipe is the `from` of the route, its steps are the steps, and its sink
+is a `to`. The xref:camel-4x-upgrade-guide-4_23.adoc#_camel_yaml_dsl_pipe_kind_pipe_support_is_deprecated[Camel 4.23
+upgrade guide] shows a Pipe and the route that does the same. Kamelets are not affected: routes use them as
+`kamelet:` endpoints.
